change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted condition
findings.body: The encoded prefix is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2)` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117`), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. On top of that, the code returns `false` when the shortcut *matches*, which is the reverse of what the matcher should do. Take `onrtac:<uuid>`: `substring(3,5)` is `"ta"`, which isn't equal to `"ac"`, so the matcher just falls through to the UUID check and passes. A token issued with the wrong grant would pass too. The assertions in `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` therefore only check that the value is `xxx:<uuid>`, not which grant issued it. Fix: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also check `items[0].length() == 6` first. Note that once this is fixed, any flow where the grant attribute isn't set (it falls back to `na`) will start failing these assertions.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check actually checks grantType again
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` passes `grantType` again, so a null `rawTokenId` is never rejected. If one gets through, `encodeTokenId` builds an id ending in `:null`. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks custom grant factories, and the shortcut length isn't checked
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is abstract with no default. Every third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` will now fail to compile or load, and a factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` (lines 75-76), which aborts server startup. The decoder also requires exactly 2 characters per segment (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-81`), but nothing checks the length of a custom shortcut. A 3-letter shortcut (which the Javadoc says is the usual form) produces token ids that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Options: validate the length (exactly 2) and non-null in `postInit` with a clear error, fix the Javadoc's "3-letters" wording, and possibly add a default implementation.

contracts.action: initToken now builds the access-token id through TokenContextEncoderProvider (prefix + ':' + UUID)
contracts.before_after: Grant paths set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on clientSessionCtx before the token is created (OAuth2GrantTypeBase:109, ROPC:134, refresh TokenManager:248, token exchange:237, pre-authorized code:82). Other paths fall back to 'na'.
contracts.visible_effect: The jti and TOKEN_ID event detail change from a UUID to something like 'onrtac:<uuid>'
contracts.failure_mode: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the grant attribute names a grant with no registered factory, which fails token issuance

summary: The PR encodes session type, token type and grant into the access-token id. I found one real test bug: the new `isAccessTokenId` matcher in `AssertEvents.java:483` reads the wrong offset and has its condition inverted, so it never checks the grant shortcut. Two smaller points: a null check in `AccessTokenContext.java:73` tests `grantType` twice and never `rawTokenId`, and the new abstract `getShortcut()` is risky for custom grant factories because nothing checks it's non-null or exactly 2 characters.
